command:description.maml:para: Adds or updates a value in a CustomFieldCollection.

Adds or updates a value identified by Id in the target collection. Accepts either a PowerShell object (Object parameter set) or a raw JSON string (Json parameter set). Honors WhatIf/Confirm and writes the updated collection.

maml:description.maml:para: The target collection to modify. Accepts input from the pipeline and may be empty.
The custom field identifier to add or update.
The value to store, provided as a PowerShell object. Used in the Object parameter set.
The value to store, provided as a raw JSON string. Used in the Json parameter set.
This cmdlet accepts a CustomFieldCollection from the pipeline.
The updated collection.

command:description.maml:para: Gets a value from a CustomFieldCollection by identifier and optionally converts it to a specific .NET type.

Retrieves the value of the specified custom field from a CustomFieldCollection. By default returns the underlying System.Text.Json.JsonElement (Raw). Use -As to convert to a specific type (for example String, Int32, DateTime). Writes the value (which may be null) to the pipeline and throws a terminating error if conversion fails.

maml:description.maml:para: The collection containing custom field values. Typically obtained from a GraphQL response. Accepts input from the pipeline.
The identifier of the custom field to retrieve.
Controls the output type. Raw returns System.Text.Json.JsonElement; other values convert to a specific .NET type.
This cmdlet accepts a CustomFieldCollection from the pipeline.
The extracted value (JsonElement for Raw, or a converted .NET type).

command:description.maml:para: Executes an AccountQuery against the Xurrent GraphQL API.
Executes a composed AccountQuery and writes the resulting Account object to the pipeline.

maml:description.maml:para: Specifies the AccountQuery to execute. This parameter determines which Account data is retrieved.
Specifies the XurrentPowerShellClient instance to use for execution. If omitted, the last created client instance will be used.
Accepts a AccountQuery object from the pipeline (by value) or by property name (property "Query").
The resulting Account object.

reference of the closure code to be selected for the request when it has been completed. Generally this reference is the snake-cased version of the name (eg. resolved_by_workaround for "Resolved by Workaround").

By default, the person selected in the Requested by field receives a notification based on the 'Desired Completion Set for Request' email template whenever the value in the Desired completion field is set, updated or removed.
Used to specify the actual date and time at which the service became available again.
Used to specify the actual date and time at which the service outage started.

command:description.maml:para: Creates a new ServiceLevelAgreement via the Xurrent GraphQL API.
Creates a new ServiceLevelAgreement and writes the resulting ServiceLevelAgreementCreatePayload object to the pipeline.

maml:description.maml:para: Identifier of the organization that pays for the service level agreement.
The name of the service level agreement.
Identifier of the service offering that specifies the conditions that apply to the service level agreement.

The Activity ID is the unique identifier by which an activity that is performed in the context of a service offering is known in the billing system of the service provider. This contains the activityIDs related to request categories.
The Agreement ID is the unique identifier by which all the activities that are performed through the coverage of the SLA are known in the billing system of the service provider.
A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation.
Used to specify how people who are to be covered by the service level agreement are to be selected.

Identifier of the account which service level managers are allowed to update the parts of the SLA that are intended to be maintained by the service level managers of the customer. More importantly, this field is used to specify whether specialists of the customer are allowed to see the requests that include this SLA in their Affected SLAs section.
Identifiers of the people who represents the customer organization for the service level agreement.

The date through which the service level agreement (SLA) will be active. The SLA expires at the end of this day if it is not renewed before then. When the SLA has expired, its status will automatically be set to "Expired".

The Rate IDs are the unique identifiers by which an effort class that is linked to a time entry when an activity was performed through the coverage of the SLA is known in the billing system of the service provider.

Represents the activityIDs for request for change types. The Activity ID is the unique identifier by which an activity that is performed in the context of a service offering is known in the billing system of the service provider.

Represents the activityIDs for standard service requests. The Activity ID is the unique identifier by which an activity that is performed in the context of a service offering is known in the billing system of the service provider.

The last day on which the service provider organization can still be contacted to terminate the service level agreement (SLA) to ensure that it expires on the intended expiry date. The Notice date field is left empty, and the Expiry date field is filled out, when the SLA is to expire on a specific date and no notice needs to be given to terminate it.

Identifiers of the organizations of the service level agreement. Only available for service level agreements where the coverage field is set to organizations_and_descendants, organizations or organizations_and_sites.
Identifiers of the people of the service level agreement. Only available for service level agreements where the coverage field is set to people.
Any additional information about the service level agreement that might prove useful.
The attachments used in the remarks field.

Identifier of the service instance that will be used to provide the service to the customer of the service level agreement. Only service instances that are linked to the same service as the selected service offering can be selected.
Identifier of the person of the service provider organization who acts as the service level manager for the customer of the service level agreement.
Identifiers of the sites of the service level agreement. Only available for service level agreements where the coverage field is set to sites or organizations_and_sites.
Identifiers of the skill pools of the service level agreement. Only available for service level agreements where the coverage field is set to skill_pools.
An identifier for the client application submitting the resource or the name of an external system.
The unique identifier of the resource in an external system.
The first day during which the service level agreement (SLA) is active.
The current status of the service level agreement (SLA).

Whether knowledge articles from the service provider should be exposed to the people covered by the service instances related to the service level agreement. Only available for service level agreements where the coverage field is set to service_instances.

command:description.maml:para: Starts a bulk data export job in Xurrent.
Starts a CSV or Excel export and writes the export token string to the pipeline.

maml:description.maml:para: Export format. Use CSV or Excel.
Line separator for CSV exports. Ignored for Excel.
Record types to include in the export.
Lower bound timestamp. Only records created or updated on or after this date are included.
Client instance to use. If omitted, the last created client instance will be used.
This cmdlet does not accept input from the pipeline.
Export token string.

command:description.maml:para: Starts a bulk data import job in Xurrent.
Uploads the specified file and starts an import for the given type. Writes the import token string to the pipeline.

maml:description.maml:para: Full file system path of the file to import.
Type of data being imported (entity name recognized by the bulk import API).
Client instance to use. If omitted, the last created client instance will be used.
This cmdlet does not accept input from the pipeline.
Import token string.

command:description.maml:para: Determines whether any authentication token associated with the client has sufficient remaining rate and cost quota.

Resolves the client (using the provided client or the active/default client) and evaluates each token. Writes True if at least one token has RequestLimit.Remaining greater than MinRateRemaining and CostLimit.Remaining greater than MinCostRemaining; otherwise writes False. Defaults: MinRateRemaining = 50, MinCostRemaining = 100.

maml:description.maml:para: The XurrentPowerShellClient instance to use. If omitted, the last created client instance will be used.
The minimum remaining request quota required for a token to qualify. Strictly greater than comparison is used. Default: 50.
The minimum remaining cost budget required for a token to qualify. Strictly greater than comparison is used. Default: 100.
This cmdlet does not accept input from the pipeline.
True if any token exceeds both thresholds; otherwise False.

command:description.maml:para: Waits for a bulk data import to complete and returns the final status.
Polls the Xurrent bulk API at a configurable interval until the import finishes or the timeout elapses, then writes the final response to the pipeline.

maml:description.maml:para: Import token returned by Start-XurrentDataImport. Accepted from the pipeline.
Interval in seconds between polling attempts. Range: 10–120. Default: 30.
Maximum wait time in seconds. Use 0 to wait indefinitely. Range: 0–900. Default: 0.
Client instance to use. If omitted, the last created client instance will be used.
Import token accepted from the pipeline.
Final import status response.
